To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) Day 7 blastocytes are not more likely to be chromosomally normal than Day 5 or Day 6 blastocytes, and (b) Day 7 embryo culture after warming of cryopreserved human oocytes is a useful strategy for increasing the number of usable blastocytes.

the proportion of Day 7 embryos in oocyte warming cycles was higher than that in fresh cycles, and the clinical outcomes of Day 7 embryo transfer were comparable to those of Day 5 and Day 6 embryo transfer in oocyte warming and fresh cycles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of extended embryo culture to day 7 on the outcome of in vitro fertilization (IVF) of cryopreserved oocytes.
the necessity of Day 7 culture in IVF of cryopreserved oocytes.
the development of blastocysts in human embryos from cryopreserved oocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Day 7 culture of cryopreserved human oocytes is not necessary.
Day 7 blastocyte culture is a good option for cryopreserved and warmed oocytes.
Day 7 culture is necessary for in vitro fertilization of cryopreservation/warmed human oocyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Day 7 embryo culture is not necessary for oocyte warming cycles.
Day 7 culture for cryopreserved/warm oocytes IVF can be performed without compromising the quality of the embryos and the clinical outcomes.
extended embryo culture to day 7 is not necessary to obtain more transfertable blastocysts for cryopreserved/warmerd oocyte IVF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Day 7 culture of cryopreserved oocytes is not necessary to obtain more blastocyst for transfer.
Day 7 culture of human embryos is necessary for oocyte warming IVF to increase the number of transferrable blastocytes.
the extended culture to day 7 is not necessary for the cryopreserved oocytes, but it can help to increase the number of usable blastcysts.
